university: Missouri University of Science and Technology

documents.unit: Teaching and Learning Center (GAI task force)
documents.title: Generative AI (GAI) Guidelines
documents.summary: A faculty task force page offering three levels of student GAI use (green, yellow, red) that instructors may adopt with icons in syllabi or per assignment. It leaves the rule to each instructor, cautions against AI checkers, and asks students who may use GAI to verify and cite.
documents.stance_why: The page says the task force produced 'guidelines that would assist S&T faculty with developing their own course policies' and that 'Instructors have academic freedom to set acceptable levels of GAI use', with three levels as options, so the document sets no stance itself and delegates.

units.why: The task force produced 'guidelines that would assist S&T faculty with developing their own course policies', so the university offers a framework and leaves the course rule to faculty: delegation (P04).
units.resolution_why: A coded P56 (framework statement), B coded P04. The passage sets no principle or rule; it says the guidelines help faculty write 'their own course policies', which is delegation. Final P04; A's governance topic kept.
units.anchor: guidelines that would assist S&T faculty with developing their own course policies

units.why: The goal sentence says the criteria are for faculty 'if they deemed necessary for their courses', so using the criteria is optional and course policy stays with faculty (P04).
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit. The source sentence ('criteria faculty could use if they deemed necessary') is a real optional-use statement for instructors, so it is kept.
units.anchor: criteria faculty could use if they deemed necessary for their courses

units.why: 'The task force produced three levels of GAI use in courses' names the tiered scheme (green, yellow, red), so P05; it states the scheme, so informs.
units.resolution_why: Actor differed (A all, B admin); the sentence describes the scheme for any reader, so all. B's extra topic default-stance dropped because the tiers set no default.
units.anchor: The task force produced three levels of GAI use in courses

units.why: The text defines the red level as 'no use of GAI is acceptable', one of the tiers (P05); it bans AI at that level, so unit_stance is prohibit, but it is a tier definition rather than a course default (P01).
units.resolution_why: Coders agreed on type, modality and stance but differed on actor (A all, B instructor) and phase (A general, B course-start). The sentence defines a tier for everyone and is not an instruction to put a statement in a syllabus, so all and general.
units.anchor: the red—no use of GAI is acceptable
units.frag_start: When an academic honesty issue is raised, a
units.frag_end: makes the case easier to address.
units.policy: Red level: no use of GAI is acceptable.
units.fit_note: Only the red level is defined in the page text; green and yellow definitions are in images not captured.

units.why: The task force 'recommends that faculty include their own written policy regarding students' GAI use', asking instructors to state a course AI policy in the syllabus (P09); 'recommends' makes it should.
units.resolution_why: Phase differed (A course-start, B before-course). Writing the policy for students is communicating expectations, so course-start.
units.anchor: faculty include their own written policy regarding students’ GAI use.

units.why: 'These categories are not intended to be comprehensive' says the levels do not cover every case, so a caveat on the tier scheme (P05).
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit. The source clause is a real scope statement about the tiers, so it is kept.
units.anchor: These categories are not intended to be comprehensive
units.fit_note: Caveat on the tiers rather than a tier definition.

units.why: The text hopes widespread use of the images 'may promote more consistent student recognition of course GAI policies', a reason for common signage that concerns communicating expectations (P09).
units.resolution_why: Both coders agreed on every code; B's longer anchor was replaced by A's shorter one. B's fit note is merged with A's.
units.anchor: may promote more consistent student recognition of course GAI policies
units.fit_note: Encourages uniform official icons across faculty so students recognize policies across courses; not a duty to state a policy.

units.why: The images 'will be included in the syllabus material provided to all faculty members by the office of Undergraduate Education' and 'automatically included in syllabi created using Simple Syllabus'; an institutional step that puts the levels in syllabi (P09).
units.anchor: included in the syllabus material provided to all faculty members
units.fit_note: The institution supplies the statement; it does not require instructors to write one.

units.why: 'Instructors have academic freedom to set acceptable levels of GAI use in their classroom' leaves the rule to each instructor and permits them to set it (P04).
units.resolution_why: Modality differed (A may, B informs) and unit_stance differed (A permit, B neutral). The sentence grants instructors the freedom to set levels, so may; it takes no position on AI use itself, so neutral. B's learning-rationale topic dropped.
units.anchor: Instructors have academic freedom to set acceptable levels of GAI use

units.why: 'students need to clearly understand the expectation from one instructor to another' gives the reason levels help: rules differ by instructor so they must be communicated (P09; P11 does not fit because it does not say permissions fail to carry over).
units.anchor: students need to clearly understand the expectation from one instructor to another
units.fit_note: States that students need clear expectations across instructors; no duty to write a statement.

units.why: 'a clear statement on the syllabus such as the red ... makes the case easier to address' ties a clear syllabus statement to academic-honesty cases; it does not classify misuse as misconduct (P36), so the nearest type is P09 with a note.
units.resolution_why: A coded P09 with a fit note, B coded UNCOVERED. The sentence is about the value of a clear syllabus statement (communicating expectations) with an enforcement benefit added; P09 is where a reader would look, so P09 with a fit note. B's uncovered_note is kept in the fit_note.
units.anchor: a clear statement on the syllabus such as the red
units.frag_start: When an academic honesty issue is raised, a
units.frag_end: makes the case easier to address.
units.fit_note: Adds that a clear syllabus statement supports academic-honesty cases (B: 'A clear syllabus AI statement makes academic honesty cases easier to handle'); no type covers this link between syllabus statements and enforcement.

units.why: 'tutoring, or the S&T Writing & Communication Center can help students operate within the rules set by the instructor' points students to human support (P72).
units.anchor: tutoring, or the S&T Writing & Communication Center can help students

units.why: 'Here are some useful examples of how GAI can be used in teaching' followed by resources (Harvard assignments, prompts, an article) supports instructors in learning about AI before setting policy (P63).
units.anchor: Here are some useful examples of how GAI can be used in teaching

units.why: 'TLC has copies you can borrow or you can check out a digital copy' offers faculty a book on teaching with AI, a faculty learning resource (P63).
units.resolution_why: Only coder A coded the book separately (B folded it into the resource unit). It is a distinct resource offer on the page, so it is kept.
units.anchor: TLC has copies you can borrow or you can check out a digital copy

units.why: 'The UM system does not endorse nor provide an AI checker' is the system's position on detectors (P39).
units.resolution_why: unit_stance differed (A neutral, B restrict). The sentence states a system position on detection software and says nothing about students' AI use, so neutral.
units.anchor: The UM system does not endorse nor provide an AI checker.

units.why: 'These have been shown to be highly unreliable and biased' gives the reason detectors are unreliable (P39).
units.resolution_why: Only coder A split this sentence out (B folded it into its next unit). It is a distinct factual claim about detectors, so it is kept.
units.anchor: These have been shown to be highly unreliable and biased.

units.why: 'Faculty are therefore cautioned against attempting to use this type of software' tells instructors not to rely on detectors; 'cautioned' makes it should-not (P39).
units.anchor: Faculty are therefore cautioned against attempting to use this type of software.

units.why: 'detection software has not been able to keep up' with updating GAIs is the supporting fact that detectors fail (P39).
units.anchor: detection software has not been able to keep up

units.why: When GAI is allowed, 'you must verify and cite all claims and information appropriately', which requires citing (P24); the verification half is coded separately.
units.anchor: you must verify and cite all claims and information appropriately
units.frag_start: When GAI is allowed you must
units.policy: When GAI is allowed, students must cite all claims and information appropriately.
units.fit_note: The sentence also requires verifying, coded as a separate unit; it requires citing claims and information, not stating that AI use itself was disclosed.

units.why: The same sentence requires students to 'verify' all claims and information when GAI is allowed, which is verifying AI output (P31).
units.anchor: you must verify and cite all claims and information appropriately
units.frag_start: When GAI is allowed you must
units.policy: When GAI is allowed, students must verify all claims and information.

units.why: 'GAI are known to hallucinate and may include bias' is a warning in the optional student statement that output can be wrong or biased (P31).
units.resolution_why: Actor and phase differed (A student/during-work, B all/general). The sentence sits in the optional statement written for students about using AI output, so student and during-work.
units.anchor: GAI are known to hallucinate and may include bias.

units.why: 'Do not blindly trust the information an AI generates' tells students to evaluate AI output critically (P31).
units.anchor: Do not blindly trust the information an AI generates.

units.why: 'You must also not adopt generated content without reflection and revision to make it your work' requires students to make submitted work their own (P29); P32 (staying primary problem-solver) is a weaker fit because the sentence is about owning the final work.
units.resolution_why: A coded P32, B coded P29. The source ends 'to make it your work', so the rule is that submitted work must become the student's own, which is P29's definition; it does not say AI must not replace thinking. Final P29.
units.anchor: not adopt generated content without reflection and revision
units.frag_start: You must also not adopt generated
units.fit_note: Also bears on student reflection and revision, which P32 covers.

units.why: 'it is recommended that each assignment ... be tagged as green, yellow, or red' recommends per-assignment level tagging when levels vary, a tier practice (P05); 'recommended' makes it should.
units.anchor: each assignment within the course or assignment be tagged as green, yellow, or red.

units.why: 'If an instructor designates different levels for assignments or projects within a course' allows the level to differ per assignment, which leaves the choice to the instructor (P04).
units.resolution_why: Only coder A found this unit. The conditional clause is a real permission to vary levels by assignment, kept. unit_stance set neutral rather than A's permit since it takes no position on AI use itself.
units.anchor: If an instructor designates different levels for assignments or projects within a course

units.why: 'These icons can be used to tag individual assignments' says the official icons may be used per assignment (P05, may).
units.resolution_why: Only coder B found this unit. The sentence is a real permission about using the tier icons per assignment, kept.
units.anchor: These icons can be used to tag individual assignments

notes: Page text describes only the red level; green and yellow definitions are in images not captured, so no units can be quoted for them. No school or computing policy found by either coder; course layer deferred. The page is a TLC task-force guideline, not a binding policy.
